subject: Overage handling & surge mitigation — proposed playbook and credit structure
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Dedicated overages last week

Hey Vanessa,

Hope you had a good week. We pulled our bill for the Dedicated pool for Dec 27–Jan 2 and saw a ~68% spike over our committed GPU-hours. The usage spike was driven by an automated nightly workflow that suddenly retried a bad job for ~4 hours. We anticipated some burst but didn’t expect the overage to be billed at full list overrun rates — that jump will blow our Q1 forecast.

Can Redwood walk us through how overages are metered (per-minute? per-GPU-hour?), whether there are protection windows for short bursts, and any options you have for smoothing/credits while we fix our pipeline? We’re in the middle of finalizing a 12-month commit and this clarity would be decisive.

Also attaching our export (acme_usage_report_Q4.csv). Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Chen
Head of ML Engineering
Acme Analytics

(Attachment: acme_usage_report_Q4.csv)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2027 11:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Dedicated overages last week

Hi Lisa — thanks for the export, that helps. High level before a call:

- Metering: Dedicated overages are billed by GPU-hour on a per-instance runtime basis with 1-minute resolution for short-lived tasks, and hourly alignment for long-running allocation (we round up partial-minute usage to the next full minute).
- Short-burst protection: we offer a 24-hour rolling buffer rule for new commits (first 30 days) and an optional surge credit for predictable workloads to absorb short spikes.
- Throttling: when you exceed commit and the pool is under pressure, requests are placed into a soft-priority queue and a throttling policy (configurable) reduces token concurrency per-request rather than hard-cutting requests.

I can propose a concrete playbook for you (credits + temporary surge cap + fallback model routing + invoicing cadence) and we can run a 30-day mitigation credit while you patch your retry loop. Does Monday 10:00 PT work for a 30-min sync?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

(Attachment: proposed_playbook_summary.pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme — overage ask / need quick pricing playbook

Team — forwarding Acme's usage and Lisa’s note. They’re close to finalizing a 12-mo Dedicated commit but this unexpected spike is causing procurement to pause. Need an approved mitigation + commercial structure we can offer ASAP (to be clear, this is for a dedicated GPU pool with a planned commit of ~120 GPU-hours/day).

Key asks from Acme: explanation of metering, short-burst protection for fast retry issues, and a one-time credit/temporary surge allowance while they fix their pipeline.

Proposed items for discussion:
- 30-day surge credit: cover up to 100 GPU-hours above commit, capped at $X — suggest we offer as a one-time concession if they sign within 10 days.
- Tiered overage rates: below 15% above commit -> low overage rate (e.g., 0.5x list), 15–50% -> 0.75x, >50% -> full list.
- Throttle config: default soft-priority queue that reduces concurrency by 40% for excess requests for up to 2 hours; emergency manual override for customers on enterprise support.
- Metering granularity confirmation: 1-minute resolution for transient jobs, hourly alignment for persistent allocation — need ops confirmation.

Rishi — legal/finance: any issues with tiered surcharges like this? Laura — finance: what credit level would you recommend tied to commit signature?

Thanks,
V

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme — overage ask / need quick pricing playbook

Vanessa — good summary. My recommended, low-friction commercial motion:

1) Immediate offer (to present to customer):
   - 30-day Surge Support Credit:
     * One-time credit that offsets the next invoice up to 100 GPU-hours (applies only to overage portion).
     * Credit redeemable if Acme executes the 12-mo commit within 10 business days.

   - Tiered Overage Pricing (applies after credit exhaustion):
     * 0–10% above commit: 0.4x list price per GPU-hour
     * 10–40% above commit: 0.75x list price per GPU-hour
     * >40% above commit: 1.0x list price per GPU-hour
   - Surge cap guardrail: automatic soft-throttle if 60% above commit sustained for >30 min; we will notify customer at 20% and 40% thresholds.

2) Operational safeguards (we can configure this for them):
   - Fallback routing: requests that exceed a configurable latency budget can be routed to a smaller, cheaper model variant (e.g., 7B quantized) to preserve throughput.
   - Auto-retry budget: we can put a temporary per-job retry ceiling (3 attempts) enforced by gateway to prevent runaway retries.
   - Metering clarification: confirm with infra — we bill in 1-minute increments for ephemeral execution; for reserved machine allocations we prorate to nearest minute with hourly caps.

3) Accounting / invoicing:
   - Provide itemized overage lines and a summary credit line on the invoice.
   - If they need predictable forecasting, offer a monthly smoothing report and projected burn rate dashboard in Console for the first 90 days.

Laura / Rishi — ok to offer that credit structure and tiered rates as a seed offer? If yes, I’ll present to Lisa and get a verbal ok.

- Aditya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Dedicated overages last week — proposal

Lisa / Tom — thanks again for the dataset and for walking through this with us. Per our internal review, here’s a concise mitigation proposal we can implement immediately if you approve: 

1) 30-day Surge Support Credit
   - Redwood will grant a one-time credit that offsets up to 100 GPU-hours of overage for your next invoice. Condition: Acme signs the 12-month Dedicated commit (120 GPU-hours/day) within 10 business days from today.

2) Tiered Overage Pricing after credit
   - 0–10% over commit: 0.4x list price/GPU-hour
   - 10–40% over commit: 0.75x list price/GPU-hour
   - >40% over commit: 1.0x list price/GPU-hour

3) Operational protections (can be turned on immediately)
   - Soft-priority throttling: reduce per-request concurrency by up to 40% for excess traffic windows, with email alerts at 20% and 40% thresholds.
   - Fallback routing: excess requests that breach a latency SLA can be routed to a quantized/smaller model to preserve throughput.
   - Gateway retry ceiling: cap retries at 3 attempts per job for 30 days to avoid runaway loops.

4) Billing and transparency
   - Overages will be visible in Console with per-route token/tokenized trace and per-GPU-hour metering. We will include an itemized credit line for the one-time Surge Support Credit on the first invoice after sign.

5) Next steps
   - If you want this protective configuration and the credit, sign the attached MOU and countersign (DocuSign link above) within 10 business days. We’ll enable the acetate mitigation settings and send a dedicated monitoring dashboard.

I’m happy to adjust credit size or tiering in exchange for a different commit length or a higher initial commit (e.g., 180 GPU-hours/day) if you prefer. Quick call? I have 10:00 PT tomorrow.

Warmly,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
